newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CRICKET-AUSTRALIA RECALLS LANGER FOR WINDIES TEST.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-AUSTRALIA RECALLS LANGER FOR WINDIES TEST.

text.p: Left-hander Justin Langer was recalled to the Australian test team after a three-year absence on Monday after scoring an unbeaten 274 at the weekend.
Team selectors also opted for Queensland opener Matthew Hayden to replace the injured Matthew Elliott for the third test against the West Indies starting on Thursday in Melbourne.
Australia will also be boosted by the return of veteran all-rounder Steve Waugh, who missed the second test because of a groin strain but is now back in top form.

Waugh batted for almost eight hours at the weekend for an unbeaten 186 that helped rescue New South Wales in a Sheffield Shield match against Queensland. His twin brother Mark, also in the test team, scored 159 in the same innings.

But the performance likely to cause most concern in West Indies ranks came in Perth, where Langer's unbeaten 274 put Western Australia in a dominant position over South Australia. Langer replaced young Tasmanian Ricky Ponting, who was dropped.
Langer, 26, has made centuries in the first innings of his last three Shield games.
Young Queensland paceman Michael Kasprowicz was dropped after going wicketless in his first two tests, leaving a batsman the likely 12th man in Melbourne.
Australia, who regained the Frank Worrell trophy in the Caribbean last year, lead the five test series 2-0 and need only a draw to retain the trophy.
Team: Mark Taylor (captain), Matthew Hayden, Mark Waugh, Steve Waugh, Justin Langer, Michael Bevan, Greg Blewett, Ian Healy (vice-captain), Shane Warne, Paul Reiffel, Jason Gillespie, Glenn McGrath
